headline: July 14 set for charge-framing hearing against Hasina and 285 others
summary: A Dhaka court has scheduled the remaining hearing for a sedition case involving the ousted Prime Minister and hundreds of others accused of anti-state activities.
details: A Dhaka court has fixed July 14 for the remaining hearing on the framing of charges in a sedition case against ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and 285 others.

The accused are alleged to have attempted to overthrow the interim government and engaged in anti-state activities. A partial hearing was held on Wednesday at the court of Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge Moin Uddin Chowdhury.
During the proceedings, 34 suspects were produced from prison and six appeared in person. Defence lawyers sought an adjournment, but the judge denied the plea, ordering the hearing to proceed.

Currently, 246 of the suspects, including Sheikh Hasina, are absconding. Other named individuals include former Khulna Jubo League leader Parvez Khan Iman and 'Joy Bangla Brigade' chief Kabirul Islam Akash.
The case was filed on March 27 last year by CID Assistant Superintendent of Police Enamul Haque. A chargesheet was submitted on July 30 and accepted by the court on August 14.

The prosecution alleges that several hundred Awami League leaders joined a Zoom meeting on December 19, 2024, where Hasina allegedly made anti-state remarks and instructed efforts to oust Chief Advisor Muhammad Yunus.

headline: 2,369 people pushed into Bangladesh by BSF since August 2024
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed reveals the scale of forced push-ins and the BGB's efforts to foil 36 recent attempts.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed informed parliament today that the Indian Border Security Force (BSF) has pushed 2,369 people into Bangladesh since August 5, 2024.
Of those pushed in, 2,175 were handed over to police stations, 183 were pushed back, and 11 were handed back to the BSF.
The minister also noted that the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has successfully foiled 36 push-in attempts since the West Bengal assembly elections.
To combat these incidents, the government has intensified surveillance using thermal imagers, night-vision devices, CCTV, and drones in sensitive border areas.
The BSF has been requested to use non-lethal weapons, and BGB-BSF director general-level conferences are being held to bring border killings down to zero.
The government has identified high-risk zones and established permanent and temporary observation posts to prevent illegal infiltration and drug trafficking.
Minister Ahmed described the killing of innocent Bangladeshi citizens by the BSF as a 'deeply tragic' violation of human rights.
Joint night patrols and prompt flag meetings at the company and battalion commander levels are being used to maintain stability and defuse tensions.
caption:
Over 2,300 people have been forced back into Bangladesh by the BSF since August.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed informed parliament today that the Indian Border Security Force (BSF) has pushed 2,369 people into Bangladesh since August 5, 2024.

Of those pushed in, 2,175 were handed over to police stations, 183 were pushed back, and 11 were handed back to the BSF.

The minister also noted that the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has successfully foiled 36 push-in attempts since the West Bengal assembly elections.

To combat these incidents, the government has intensified surveillance using thermal imagers, night-vision devices, CCTV, and drones in sensitive border areas.

The BSF has been requested to use non-lethal weapons, and BGB-BSF director general-level conferences are being held to bring border killings down to zero.

The government has identified high-risk zones and established permanent and temporary observation posts to prevent illegal infiltration and drug trafficking.

Minister Ahmed described the killing of innocent Bangladeshi citizens by the BSF as a 'deeply tragic' violation of human rights.

Joint night patrols and prompt flag meetings at the company and battalion commander levels are being used to maintain stability and defuse tensions.
